$comment: Hand-reviewed repairs for head values that the printed Kurlar catalogues get wrong.
Every entry here was confirmed to be a PRINTING error, not an extraction error: the
PDF words sit correctly inside their table columns (verified by coordinate, see
extract_pump_curves.py) and the printed digits themselves contradict physics —
either head rising as flow rises within one pump, or head falling as identical
`printed` is asserted against what the extractor actually read. If a catalogue is
ever replaced and the value changes, the correction refuses to apply and extraction
fails loudly rather than silently rewriting new data.
ASK KURLAR TO CONFIRM these values. They are the best reconstruction available from
the surrounding table, not manufacturer-supplied figures.

motorCorrections.reason: Typo in the printed motor table: a stray comma inside the number. The 400 V and 415 V rows of the same motor read 87.8 and 85.7, and current falls as voltage rises throughout the range, so 90.3 A is the only reading consistent with its own row. This is a transcription repair, not a reconstruction.

corrections.reason: Breaks the row (317 m at 6 m3/h cannot rise to 375 m at 9 m3/h) and the column (/29=265, /31=280). Column runs +9..10 m per stage throughout. Linear interpolation between the two good neighbours gives 272.5. Likely a 2->3 digit slip; note 375 is the legitimate value 11 rows further down at /41.

Breaks the row: 269 m at 4 m3/h is below the 270 m printed at 8 m3/h. Column runs +11 m per stage; anchors /24=265 and /27=300 interpolate to 276.7. The printed 269/279 for /25 and /26 look copied from the 8 m3/h column (270/280).
Same fault as /25: 279 m at 4 m3/h is below the 280 m printed at 8 m3/h. Interpolating /24=265 to /27=300 gives 288.3.

Breaks the column (/17=344 > /18=342, but adding a stage must add head) and the row (342 m shut-off is below the 355 m printed at 20 m3/h). Anchors /17=344 and /19=382 interpolate to 363, matching the column's steady +19..20 m per stage.

Rows /17..21 of this one column advance by +8 m per stage where the column runs +28. Every other column in the same rows continues correctly (+29/+25/+23/+20/+18/+12), so a single column was mis-typeset. On all good rows this column sits 1-2 m under the shut-off column (/14 408/406, /15 436/435, /16 466/465); shut-off here is 495.
Same mis-typeset column block as /17. Shut-off for this row is 524.
Same mis-typeset column block as /17. Shut-off for this row is 553.
Same mis-typeset column block as /17. Shut-off for this row is 582. The printed 497 also breaks the row, sitting below the 509 m printed at 80 m3/h.
Same mis-typeset column block as /17. Shut-off for this row is 611. The printed 505 also breaks the row, sitting below the 534 m printed at 80 m3/h.

exclusions.reason: KP-895 rows /21../24 are unreliable across the whole curve, not in one column. Their per-stage increments are a flat ~9-10 m in EVERY flow column, whereas a real curve falls off with flow — this family runs +20/+20/+18/+15/+13/+10/+8 for its first twenty rows. Columns 0, 1 and 2 are all affected and /21 additionally breaks the row (432 m shut-off below 471 m at 20 m3/h) and the column (/22=426 < /21=471). Reconstructing these would mean inventing four complete pump curves, so they are withheld from selection instead. KP-895/01../20 are unaffected and remain available.
See KP-895/21 — same unreliable trailing block.
See KP-895/21 — same unreliable trailing block. Also breaks the row: 381 m at 20 m3/h is below the 393 m printed at 40 m3/h.
See KP-895/21 — same unreliable trailing block. Also breaks the row: 336 m at 20 m3/h is below the 402 m printed at 40 m3/h.
